name: Mines
intro: A short path through Mines: what the numbers mean and how to use flags, then the 1-2-1 and 1-1 patterns and what to do when you have to guess.

units.name: How Mines works
units.blurb: The numbers, flags and safe squares.

lessons.title: Reading the numbers
lessons.summary: Every number in Mines counts the mines in the eight squares around it. Learn to read them, find certain mines and open the squares a flag makes safe.
lessons.wrap: Numbers find mines, and flags make squares safe. Next: a quick rules check.

steps.text:
The field hides mines under covered squares. Each open square shows how many of its eight neighbours, diagonals included, are mines. A blank square has none, so the game opens everything around it for you.

Uncover every safe square to win.
The highlighted 1 touches exactly one covered square. Its one mine must be there.
steps.prompt: Tap the mine next to the highlighted 1.
steps.wrong: Count the covered squares touching the highlighted 1. There’s only one.
steps.done: That’s a mine. A number with as many covered neighbours as its value tells you they’re all mines.

steps.text: That mine is now flagged. The highlighted 1 already touches the flag, so it has all the mines it needs.
steps.prompt: Tap every other covered square around the highlighted 1. They’re all safe.
steps.wrong: Look only at the covered squares touching the highlighted 1.
steps.done: All safe. On the real field, tapping a number whose mines are all flagged opens them in one go.

steps.prompt: Tap the mine next to the highlighted 1 in the bottom-left.
steps.wrong: Which covered square does that 1 touch?
steps.done: Right: it was the only covered square that 1 could see.

steps.prompt: Which squares does a number count?
options: All eight around it, diagonals included

units.name: Rules check
units.blurb: Five questions on the rules. Pass to unlock the patterns.

lessons.title: Mines rules check
lessons.summary: Test your Mines rules: what the numbers mean, blank squares, the safe first tap, finding certain mines and using flags.
lessons.wrap: Rules check passed. Now for the patterns.

steps.prompt: An open square shows 2. What does it mean?
options: Two of the eight squares around it are mines
The nearest mine is two squares away
steps.explain: Two of its eight neighbours are mines.

steps.prompt: Two 1s on this field touch just one covered square each. Tap both mines.
steps.wrong: Look for a 1 with only one covered square beside it.

steps.prompt: What happens when you uncover a blank square?
options: Every square around it opens automatically
steps.explain: A blank has no mines around it, so the game opens its neighbours for you.

steps.prompt: The flag in the corner is correct. Tap the two squares it proves safe.
steps.wrong: Look at the two 1s touching the flag. They already have their mine.

steps.prompt: Can your first tap on BoardGameSite be a mine?
steps.explain: No. The mines are laid after your first tap, never on it or next to it.

units.name: Patterns and guessing
units.blurb: The 1-2-1, the 1-1, and what to do when the numbers can’t decide.

lessons.title: The 1-2-1 pattern
lessons.summary: Along a straight edge, 1-2-1 always means mines opposite both 1s and a safe square opposite the 2. Learn to spot it and use it.
lessons.wrap: Mines opposite the 1s, safe opposite the 2. Its cousin 1-2-2-1 works the same way: mines opposite the 2s, safe opposite the 1s. Next: the 1-1.

steps.text:
Along a straight edge of open squares, look for the numbers 1, 2, 1 in a row.

The 2 needs two mines in the three squares above it. If both were next to each other, one of the 1s would touch two mines. So the mines sit opposite both 1s, and the square opposite the 2 is safe.

steps.wrong: The mines are directly opposite the two 1s.

steps.prompt: Tap the square the 1-2-1 proves safe.
steps.wrong: It’s the one directly opposite the 2.

steps.prompt: Tap the safe square opposite the 2.
steps.wrong: Find the 1, 2, 1 along the edge of the opening, then look straight past the 2.
steps.done: Spotted. With practice you’ll see 1-2-1 at a glance.

lessons.title: The 1-1 pattern
lessons.summary: Two 1s side by side, starting at the edge of the field, share one mine. Learn to find the safe square that the 1-1 pattern gives you.
lessons.wrap: The first 1 sees two squares, the second sees three: the extra square is safe. Next: what to do when the numbers can’t decide.

steps.text:
Look at the two highlighted 1s against the left edge. The first touches only two covered squares, and one of them is a mine.

The second 1 touches those same two squares plus one more. It already has its mine among the shared two, so the extra square is safe.

steps.prompt: Tap the square the second 1 sees but the first one can’t.
steps.wrong: The first 1 sees the two squares above the corner. Which square does only the second 1 see?

steps.prompt: Find the 1-1 against the right edge and tap the square it proves safe.
steps.wrong: Start from the 1 in the right-hand corner and the 1 next to it.
steps.done: Right. It also works against an area you’ve already opened, not just the edge of the field.

steps.prompt: Why is that extra square safe?
options: The second 1’s mine is in the squares it shares with the first 1
steps.explain: The shared squares already hold the second 1’s mine. Comparing what two numbers share solves many tricky spots.

lessons.title: When to guess
lessons.summary: Sometimes the numbers in Mines can’t decide between two squares. Learn to finish every certain move first, then guess as wisely as you can.
lessons.wrap: Finish the logic, then guess, and use the mine counter near the end. You’re ready for a real field.

steps.text: Most of this field is solved, and the flags are correct. Two spots are left: the top-left corner and the bottom right.
Before you guess anything, make every move that logic gives you.
steps.prompt: Tap the square in the bottom right that’s certain to be safe.
steps.wrong: One of the 1s touches only one of the two covered squares, so that one is the mine. The other is safe.
steps.done: Safe. Always clear the certain squares first.

steps.text: Now the top-left corner: two covered squares. The highlighted numbers touch both of them.
steps.prompt: Can the numbers tell you which one is the mine?
steps.explain: No. Every number that sees one also sees the other. Mines are placed at random, so now and then you have to guess.

steps.prompt: When should you make a guess like that?
options: As soon as you see it
After every certain move on the field is done
steps.explain: Last. If you guess early and lose, the safe squares you hadn’t opened yet are wasted. When you do guess earlier in a game, pick a square that would open up the most if it’s safe, often one away from the tangle.

steps.prompt: The counter says 1 mine is left. One way the last squares could work needs 1 mine, another needs 2. Which is right?
steps.explain: Only the pattern with 1 mine fits the counter. Near the end, counting mines can solve a spot the numbers alone can’t.
